create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a Machine-to-Machine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer tokens are stateless and replayable within their validity window unless additional one-time semantics are layered on top.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT/OIDC token model in Logto docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token for ordinary JWT bearer access tokens as a vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer tokens are statelessly validated; documentation does not describe jti replay tracking for normal JWT access tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same JWT is not by itself evidence of a replay vulnerability in this platform.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs retain previously granted scopes until expiration even after user permissions are reduced.
oidc_jwt.note: Only newly issued tokens reflect reduced permissions; old-token acceptance before expiry is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, refresh or later issuance cannot add scopes that were not requested in the original authorization flow.
oidc_jwt.note: A missing newly granted scope after refresh is expected unless a new authorization flow is performed.

oidc_jwt.description: Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow for user authentication.
oidc_jwt.note: Use refresh token flow to obtain organization tokens; direct code-flow absence is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange is disabled by default for applications and must be explicitly enabled.
oidc_jwt.note: A token-exchange rejection on a default app is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not modify already-issued JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect updated scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Using an old token after a role change is expected to preserve old claims until expiry.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Tests expecting JWT claims/audience behavior must request a resource or organization context.

oidc_jwt.description: If organization_id is omitted from the token request, only global roles and permissions are evaluated.
oidc_jwt.note: This is expected behavior, not an authorization bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct sign-in fails because the connector is missing or disabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: A redirect to the normal sign-in page is expected and should not be treated as flow confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified in the authorization/token request, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: JWT-specific validation attacks are not applicable to these opaque tokens; use introspection or userinfo instead.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep previously granted scopes until they expire, even after user permissions are reduced.
oidc_jwt.note: Only newly issued tokens reflect reduced permissions immediately.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to an existing Logto user account when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merging by matching email is documented behavior, not necessarily a collision bug.

oidc_jwt.description: A new user signing in with a new enterprise SSO identity gets a new Logto user account automatically created and populated from IdP data.
oidc_jwt.note: Automatic account creation for new enterprise identities is expected.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Logto issues JWT access tokens only when a specific API resource or organization context is requested. If no resource is specified, the access token is opaque and primarily for /oidc/me or introspection. For oidc_jwt tests that require JWT claim inspection or audience validation, the fuzzer MUST request a resource (or organization token context) during token issuance; otherwise tests may exercise opaque-token behavior instead of JWT validation.

The resource parameter must EXACTLY match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). Logto does not support wildcard, prefix, or partial matching for resource indicators. For I5 audience-binding tests, use exact registered URIs only; do not assume shortened or pattern values will match.

Scope names must EXACTLY match the permission names defined for the API resource. There is no wildcard or prefix matching. For I5 multi-scope tests, the fuzzer MUST request the full permission strings; values like 'read' will not match 'read:elections'.

For global API resources, an access token can only include scopes that were requested in the ORIGINAL OAuth authorization flow. Even after permissions are enlarged, refresh-token issuance can only return a subset of the originally requested scopes. For I3/I5 permission-change tests, if testing enlarged permissions on global API resources, the fuzzer MUST run a NEW authorization flow rather than relying on refresh or later token issuance.

For downscoped permission changes, existing JWTs keep old scopes until they expire; only newly issued tokens reflect reduced permissions. For I3 config-tightening tests, the fuzzer MUST obtain a NEW token after the change and MUST NOT treat continued acceptance of an old pre-change JWT as stale-policy vulnerability.

Organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. For organization-scoped I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST include organization_id in the token request; otherwise a pass/fail result reflects global authorization, not organization binding.

Organization permissions and organization-level API permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in a single authorization model. For I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST compare like-for-like permission models and must not interpret rejection of mixed global/organization scopes as a security bug.

Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. You must first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters, or use client_credentials. For organization-token tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT expect the initial authorization_code exchange to directly return the final organization JWT.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any RFC 8693 token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled in application settings; otherwise failures are expected configuration errors, not security behavior.

For token exchange using personal access tokens, subject_token_type must be urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. For impersonation-style exchanges, subject_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. The fuzzer MUST use the exact documented token type string for each subject token source; mismatches are setup errors.

OIDC token, revocation, and introspection endpoints require application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded bodies to /oidc/token, /oidc/token/revocation, and /oidc/token/introspection.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWT consumers, include a CONTROL token request/login in the same scenario using a valid token context. Without a control, rejection may reflect broken client/app/resource setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Logto validates issuer against the tenant OIDC issuer (https://<tenant>/oidc) and signatures against /oidc/jwks. For I1 trust-anchor and issuer-substitution tests, the oracle MUST treat issuer and JWKS as tenant-fixed values; Logto does not support customizing issuer or JWKS URI, so any alternate issuer/JWKS should be rejected by design.

Current SDK sign-out behavior is effectively global sign-out of the centralized Logto session, but grants with offline_access are not revoked by end-session and may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. For I2/I3 logout tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish browser-session logout from token/grant revocation; a still-valid refresh-token chain after end-session is not necessarily a vulnerability.

Default grant TTL is 180 days, and if offline_access is granted, end-session does not revoke that app grant by default. Do not interpret successful refresh or continued token exchange after browser logout as an automatic freshness failure unless the grant/token was explicitly revoked or expired.

If a default API resource is configured, omitting resource may still yield a JWT for that default audience when openid is not included; if openid is included and no resource is present, Logto may issue an opaque token for userinfo. For I5 empty_audience and audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control both resource and scope/openid presence to avoid misclassifying default-audience behavior as audience bypass.

The OIDC token endpoint /oidc/token uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded bodies for authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, and token_exchange grants; JSON bodies are not documented and may fail.
oidc_jwt.source: Core Service OIDC provider docs; token request examples in global API resources, organization permissions, organization-level API resources, PAT, impersonation docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, include a CONTROL token request that should succeed under the same client/resource setup. A failed attack request alone is ambiguous because Logto may issue opaque tokens when no resource is specified, and opaque tokens are not JWTs.
oidc_jwt.source: Opaque token docs; global API resources docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: To obtain a JWT access token for API testing, the fuzzer MUST request a resource or organization context. If no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT. JWT-specific attacks against access tokens are invalid on opaque-token flows.
oidc_jwt.source: Opaque token docs; global API resources docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, the resource parameter must EXACTLY match the registered API identifier/resource indicator. Logto documents exact URI matching; do not use prefixes, shortened forms, or wildcard-like variants.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested scope names must EXACTLY match permission names defined in the API resource. Logto does not support wildcard or prefix matching for scopes; values like 'read' do not match 'read:elections'.

For organization-scoped authorization tests, the fuzzer MUST include organization_id in the token request. Without organization_id, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced.

For user authorization-code flows, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code exchange. The fuzzer MUST use refresh_token flow to obtain organization tokens for user-based organization tests; failure to get an organization token directly from code flow is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Organization token warning fragment; organization permissions docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not retroactively modified. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens. A valid coherence test must compare a fresh token issued after the config/role change, not continued use of an old token.

For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were already within the originally requested scope set. To test newly granted permissions, the fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow if the new scopes were not part of the original request.

An access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. For I5 escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish between broker over-granting and a new authorization request that legitimately asked for broader scopes.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running RFC 8693 tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' is expected and not a security finding.

For token exchange tests using PATs, subject_token_type must be urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. For impersonation/subject-token style exchanges, subject_token_type is documented as urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. The fuzzer MUST use the documented token type for each subject token class.
oidc_jwt.source: Personal access token docs; user impersonation docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token exchange tests on confidential clients, Logto documents client authentication via HTTP Basic auth at /oidc/token; for public clients, client_id is sent in the form body. The fuzzer MUST authenticate the client in one of these documented ways or failures are setup errors.
oidc_jwt.source: Personal access token docs; user impersonation docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, compare exchanged-token scopes/claims against the original authorization intent. PAT-obtained and refresh-token-obtained access tokens are documented as equivalent in authorization behavior, so differences between those grant sources alone are not bugs.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on Logto-issued JWTs, the verifier MUST validate iss against the tenant issuer from /.well-known/openid-configuration or the fixed /oidc issuer. Do not treat acceptance of a token without issuer checking in sample backend code as a Logto broker flaw; issuer validation is part of the relying-party implementation guidance.
oidc_jwt.source: Validate access tokens docs; OIDC discovery docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience tests on Logto-issued JWTs, some sample validation code intentionally disables library-level audience verification and instructs developers to verify audience manually based on permission model. The fuzzer MUST test the actual audience checks in the target API logic, not assume the JWT library enforces aud automatically.
oidc_jwt.source: Validate access tokens docs across Node/Ruby/Python/.NET/Rust

oidc_jwt.constraint: For organization token validation, the fuzzer MUST validate both permissions (scope) and context (audience and organization_id). A token with correct scopes but wrong or missing organization context is invalid by documented design.
oidc_jwt.source: Validate token and permissions fragment; organization-level API resources docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Opaque tokens cannot be used as organization tokens. The fuzzer MUST not run organization-context JWT tests against opaque tokens obtained without resource/organization parameters.

Current Logto SDK sign-out behavior is effectively global sign-out: it redirects to /session/end and confirms logout. If offline_access was granted, end-session does not revoke that app grant by default; refresh-token-backed grants can remain valid until grant TTL expiry. The fuzzer MUST not treat surviving offline_access grants after browser sign-out as an automatic I2 violation without explicit token revocation testing.

Logto grant TTL defaults to 180 days for offline_access-backed grants. End-session clears centralized session but may leave refresh-token grants valid. Freshness tests must distinguish browser-session termination from token/grant revocation.

For re-authentication tests, prompt=login forces credential entry and bypasses SSO; when offline_access is requested, Logto recommends prompt=login consent. The fuzzer SHOULD use prompt=login for tests that require guaranteed fresh user interaction rather than silent SSO reuse.

Logto supports PKCE on the authorization flow and its SDK conventions require code_challenge_method=S256. For authorization-code tests, the fuzzer SHOULD send PKCE parameters consistently; failures caused by missing or mismatched code_verifier/code_challenge are flow-setup errors, not broker vulnerabilities.
oidc_jwt.source: Core Service enabled features; SDK conventions docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience-binding tests, the `resource` parameter in `/oidc/auth` and `/oidc/token` MUST exactly match the registered API identifier/resource indicator URI. Logto documents exact-match semantics only; prefixes or shortened values are not wildcards. For multi-resource or cross-provider tests, use distinct exact URIs and never use `*` as a wildcard audience.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested `scope` values MUST exactly match permission names defined in Logto. Logto explicitly states prefixes and shortened versions do not work as wildcards. In multi-identity scenarios, do NOT use wildcard-like scope values; request the exact permission strings under test.

For I2 freshness tests against JWT access tokens, include a CONTROL token request that should succeed alongside the attack token. Use valid time claims such as `iat={{now_epoch}}` and `exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}` for the control. Without a control, a failed attack token cannot be distinguished from broken client/app/resource setup.

For I5 tests that require JWT-format access tokens, the authorization request MUST include a `resource` parameter or rely on a configured default API resource. If no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT, which changes validation behavior and invalidates JWT-specific test assumptions.

For I5 organization-token tests, organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. Logto requires a second `/oidc/token` call using `grant_type=refresh_token` plus `organization_id` (and optionally `resource`) to obtain an organization JWT. Do not treat the initial code exchange token as the organization token oracle.

For I5 organization RBAC tests, `organization_id` controls whether organization roles are evaluated. If omitted, only global roles/permissions are considered. Therefore, tests for organization-level API resources or organization permissions MUST include `organization_id`; tests for global-only behavior MUST omit it.

For I5 permission-change and config-tightening sequences, Logto JWTs are immutable after issuance. Existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry; only newly issued tokens reflect reduced permissions. A valid test must obtain a NEW token after the change and compare outcomes, not reuse the old token.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, newly granted scopes will NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set. To test newly granted permissions, the fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow requesting those scopes, not rely on refresh alone.

For I5 organization permission enlargement tests, new permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but only within the originally requested scope set. If the new permission was not originally requested, the fuzzer MUST start a new authorization flow including that scope.

For I3 sign-out and session-coherence tests, Logto sign-out is multi-layered: clearing client tokens only signs out the local app, while redirecting to `/oidc/session/end` clears the centralized Logto session. Tests must distinguish local token deletion from IdP session termination; otherwise SSO reauthentication behavior will be misinterpreted.

For I2 revocation/logout tests with `offline_access`, end-session does not revoke the app grant by default. Refresh-token-based authorization may continue until grant expiry unless the token/grant is explicitly revoked. Do not assume browser logout alone invalidates refresh-based access.

For I3 direct sign-in tests using `direct_sign_in`, failure to find or enable the target connector causes Logto to fall back to the standard sign-in page by design. The oracle must detect fallback vs successful direct IdP initiation and must not treat fallback as a security bypass.

For I3 auth-flow parameter tests, `ui_locales`, `first_screen`, `identifier`, and `login_hint` only affect the current interaction and do not permanently change tenant settings. Tests must not infer persistent configuration changes from a single authorization request.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on the resource server side, Logto documentation shows issuer must match the tenant OIDC issuer exactly (`https://<tenant>/oidc`) and JWKS must come from `/oidc/jwks` or discovery. Trust-anchor substitution tests must keep the issuer fixed to the tenant value and vary only the signing key source to avoid trivial issuer mismatch failures.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications. SAML apps: /api/saml-applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto does NOT support ROPC (password grant). User login MUST go through the OIDC authorization code flow (start_oidc_auth → exchange_code_for_token). For machine/service login, use client_credentials grant via login_with_jwt with a Machine-to-Machine application. Do NOT use login_with_password — the /api/sign-in endpoint is a browser Experience API, not a REST API.
